Hi Lena / Novacare privacy team —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the outstanding DPA/privacy items so we can keep momentum on the evaluation and make sure the legal/security reviewers have what they need. Below are the action items we heard from your side and the asks from your privacy team: 

Action items (Novacare asks):
- Confirm Data Controller vs. Processor roles for the envisioned integration (Ingestion of patient records via API + embeddings + ephemeral KV cache).
- Subprocessor list and notification cadence (you asked about advance notice vs. immediate notice).
- Breach notification timing and what constitutes "confirmed" vs "suspected" incidents.
- Data residency options (GCP regions in us-east/us-west vs. eu-central).
- Logs & retention: what logs we retain by default (request metadata, access logs, inference logs, KV cache TTL) and whether retention is configurable per-customer.
- PII handling and options to delete training/retention traces on request.

1) I attached our current DPA (RDW_DPA_current.pdf) and the security questionnaire you shared (Novacare_Sec_Questionnaire.pdf). Please confirm receipt.
2) If you can annotate or highlight the highest-priority items in the questionnaire, we’ll prioritize those fields first.

4) If you want a formal DPA redline, we can produce one; otherwise we can provide bullet-point position statements for faster review.

Please let me know whether Novacare prefers a redline or a position memo. I’ve looped in Marcus Lin (security) and Marissa Cole (legal) for the detailed responses.

Thanks, Olga — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our legal/privacy reviewers after a quick pass: 

1) Controller/Processor: For our intended use (Novacare supplies patient records via API; Redwood returns embeddings and analysis), we are treating Novacare as Controller and Redwood as Processor. We will, however, need explicit language confirming that Redwood will not use customer data to improve models or for any training unless we opt in.

2) Subprocessors: We need the full list of subprocessors and your proposed notification window. Our preference is at least 14 days' notice before adding a new subprocessor that will process PHI-equivalent data. If you cannot do 14 days, indicate the shortest possible notice and whether emergency substitutions are possible.

3) Breach notice: Our compliance team expects a maximum of 48 hours for notification of confirmed breaches affecting Novacare data. For suspected incidents we asked for timely updates and a follow-up with root-cause + mitigation plan within 7 days.

4) Residency: We need to lock to us-east or us-west for all Novacare production data. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports region pinning within Private/Dedicated and the hosted product?

5) Logs & retention: Please confirm the default retention window for request & inference logs and whether we can apply a 30-day TTL for logs and 365 days for customer content.

6) Evidence: please share SOC 2 / ISO summary and your subprocessors CSV.

Attached: a brief annotations spreadsheet from our privacy lead (we attached in case you've not received).

Lena Hart

Hi team —

Thanks for the clear write-up, Olga. Below are concise answers we can share with Novacare; happy to convert into a redline if they prefer. I’ve also attached the redline and our SOC2 summary.

Summary answers (to share with Novacare):
- Controller / Processor: Redwood will act as Processor. We will include explicit no-training language: Redwood will not use customer-provided data to improve any public or internal models unless the customer provides written opt-in.

- Subprocessors / notification: We maintain a current subprocessors registry (link attached in Drive). For commercial customers we provide 7 days' notice for planned additions; for customers requiring longer notice we can negotiate a 14-day notice clause in the DPA. Emergency substitutions (security patching, provider decommissioning) will be allowed with immediate notification and retrospective justification; these are rare and documented.

- Breach notification timeline: We commit to notifying Novacare within 48 hours of confirmation for incidents materially impacting Novacare data. For suspected incidents we will notify within 24 hours with initial findings and provide a root-cause + mitigation plan within 7 business days.

- Data residency: Hosted API supports region pinning for enterprise accounts; Dedicated and Private deployments support hard region pinning. We can commit Novacare to us-east or us-west for production under a Dedicated deployment.

- Logs & retention: Default retention windows: request & inference logs = 90 days; KV cache entries TTL = configurable per-customer (default 24 hours); customer content retention = configurable (default 365 days). We can implement a 30-day log TTL and 365-day content retention as a contractual configuration for Novacare.

- Evidence: Attached is RDW_SOC2_summary.pdf and a redline DPA (RDW_DPA_redline_Novacare_v1.pdf). The live subprocessors CSV and SOC documents are available via the Drive link I’ll share with the customer; if Novacare needs an authority-to-access, we can route via their portal.

Next steps I suggest we present to Novacare:
1) Send the bullets above as a position memo (fast).
2) Offer a DPA redline if they want to proceed to contract review; I attached a redline for convenience.
3) Confirm which deployment mode they plan to use (hosted enterprise vs. Dedicated) — if Dedicated, we can include regional pinning language directly.

Olga — if you agree, I’ll send the memo + attach the redline and SOC2 summary.

Marcus Lin
